An estimate: the signal reaches in a circle, not along your walls, so it may also count part of the next room (walls help). Signal strength wobbles by about 10 dB. Fine-tune with \"Calibrate at the edge\".

dBm is signal strength, not distance. You type it without the minus: a smaller number means a stronger signal, so you have to be closer. Each beacon is louder or quieter, so the values below are worked out from your beacon\'s signal at 1 m. 30 is only the limit: right next to the phone most beacons read about 20 dB above their 1 m signal.
Your beacon\'s 1 m signal isn\'t known yet, so a typical %1$d dBm is assumed. Pick the beacon again (if it announces it) or measure it in 📐.

Rough guides only: your body, walls, which pocket the phone is in and the beacon\'s power shift readings by about 10 dB. Below about 45 it may flip between near and away. Best: sit where you\'ll be and use \"Calibrate at my spot\". A tablet in beacon mode reads a little weaker than a dedicated beacon. Across walls and floors Bluetooth is unreliable: for a whole home, use the Wi-Fi signal instead.

Shorter waits react sooner but may flip while you walk past. The scan only speeds up near a place (its beacon heard, or its \"Listen harder\" zone), so a fast place costs little battery while you\'re away. Battery saver also wakes the app less often (every 15 s) while near. While the phone sits idle, Android may check less often than set; a lock in progress helps.
